question.text: A stock broker dealing in derivatives must maintain the following books of accounts:

answer.text: Register of transactions, clients' ledger, margin deposit book, daily sauda register, and contract notes
Only a profit and loss statement
No specific books are required if audited annually

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (Stock Brokers) Regulations and related circulars, stock brokers — including those dealing in derivatives — are required to maintain a defined set of books of accounts and records. Industry practice and the broker-regulation requirements include a register of transactions, clients' ledger, margin deposit records, daily sauda/trade register, and contract notes issued to clients. These records support trade verification, audit, inspection and client-grievance resolution. The Trap: Maintaining only a profit and loss statement, only client contact details, or relying solely on an annual audit would be wholly inadequate. The required record-keeping is granular and trade-level. Note: The detailed list of books (register of transactions, clients' ledger, margin deposit book, daily sauda register, contract notes) is not enumerated in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages — those pages refer generally to maintenance of books and to trade confirmation slips / exercise notices being retained for five years. The framing above reflects general stock-broker record-keeping requirements rather than a workbook citation.
